tools.name: files_1mcp_create_directory
tools.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation.

tools.name: files_1mcp_directory_tree
tools.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure.

tools.name: files_1mcp_edit_file
tools.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made.

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

tools.name: files_1mcp_get_file_info
tools.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type.

path.description: The path to the file or directory

tools.name: files_1mcp_get_pwd
tools.description: Returns the current working directory (pwd), which is used as the base for relative paths.

tools.name: files_1mcp_list_directory
tools.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes.

sortBy.description: Sorting mode: default (directories first), name, or type

tools.name: files_1mcp_list_directory_info
tools.description: Returns information about the filesystem server.

tools.name: files_1mcp_move_file
tools.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation.

destination.description: The destination file or directory path

source.description: The source file or directory path

tools.name: files_1mcp_read_binary_file
tools.description: Read a binary file and return its contents as base64 encoded string.

path.description: The path to the binary file

tools.name: files_1mcp_read_file
tools.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read.

endLine.description: Ending line number (1-indexed) for reading a specific range

maxSize.description: Maximum file size in bytes to read (default: no limit)

startLine.description: Starting line number (1-indexed) for reading a specific range

tools.name: files_1mcp_read_multiple_files
tools.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files.

ignoreErrors.description: Silently skip files that cannot be read instead of including error messages

includeMetadata.description: Prepend file metadata (size, last modified) before each file's content

paths.description: Array of file paths to read

separator.description: Separator string inserted between file contents (default: '---')

tools.name: files_1mcp_search_files
tools.description: Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern. Searches through all subdirectories from the starting path.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return

searchContents.description: Search file contents instead of just names

tools.name: files_1mcp_write_file
tools.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning.

content.description: The content to write to the file

createDirectories.description: Create parent directories if they don't exist

tools.name: tasks_1mcp_tasks_add
tools.description: Add new tasks with a specific status. It's faster and cheaper if you use this in batch. User can add atomically while AI works using the CLI add tool

index.description:
0-based index to place the tasks. e.g.:
- 0 for "Do this next"
- Omit to place at the end ("Do this later")

source_id.description:
Source ID from task_setup() response
- Defaults to most recent in the workspace if not provided
- Try to always provide it!
- If you don't have it, ask the user for a file path and call task_setup()

status.description:
You might need to infer it from the context:
- "To Do" for tasks coming up next (e.g. "Do X next")
- "In Progress" for what you'll do now (e.g. "First do X")
- "Reminders" instructions for you (the AI) to be constantly reminded of
- "Notes" to collect non-actionable notes

tools.name: tasks_1mcp_tasks_search
tools.description: Search tasks from specific statuses with optional text & ID filtering

ids.description: Optional list of task IDs to search for

limit.description: Maximum number of results (only for really large task lists)

source_id.description:
Source ID from task_setup() response
- Defaults to most recent in the workspace if not provided
- Try to always provide it!
- If you don't have it, ask the user for a file path and call task_setup()

statuses.description: Specific statuses to get. Gets all if omitted

items.description:
You might need to infer it from the context:
- "To Do" for tasks coming up next (e.g. "Do X next")
- "In Progress" for what you'll do now (e.g. "First do X")
- "Reminders" instructions for you (the AI) to be constantly reminded of
- "Notes" to collect non-actionable notes

terms.description: Search terms to filter tasks by text or status (case-insensitive, OR logic, no regex or wildcards)

tools.name: tasks_1mcp_tasks_setup
tools.description:
Initializes an source file from a path
- Always call once per conversation when asked to use these tools
- Ask the user to clarify the file path if not given, before calling this tool
- Creates the file if it does not exist
- Returns the source ID for further use
- Use mcp-tasks tools when the user mentions new or updated tasks

workspace.description: Workspace/project directory path (provided by the IDE or use $PWD)

tools.name: tasks_1mcp_tasks_summary
tools.description: Get per-status task counts and the WIP task(s). Redundant right after tasks_add/tasks_update

source_id.description:
Source ID from task_setup() response
- Defaults to most recent in the workspace if not provided
- Try to always provide it!
- If you don't have it, ask the user for a file path and call task_setup()

tools.name: tasks_1mcp_tasks_update
tools.description: Update tasks in bulk by ID to a different status. Returns complete summary no need to call tasks_summary afterwards. Prevents AI accidentally rename or deleting tasks during mass updates, not even possible

index.description:
0-based index to place the tasks. e.g.:
- 0 for "Do this next"
- Omit to place at the end ("Do this later")

source_id.description:
Source ID from task_setup() response
- Defaults to most recent in the workspace if not provided
- Try to always provide it!
- If you don't have it, ask the user for a file path and call task_setup()

anyOf.description:
You might need to infer it from the context:
- "To Do" for tasks coming up next (e.g. "Do X next")
- "In Progress" for what you'll do now (e.g. "First do X")
- "Reminders" instructions for you (the AI) to be constantly reminded of
- "Notes" to collect non-actionable notes

status.description:
You might need to infer it from the context:
- "To Do" for tasks coming up next (e.g. "Do X next")
- "In Progress" for what you'll do now (e.g. "First do X")
- "Reminders" instructions for you (the AI) to be constantly reminded of
- "Notes" to collect non-actionable notes
- "Deleted" when they want these removed
- Updating tasks to In Progress moves others to To Do, finishing a In Progress task moves the first Done to In Progress
